headline: Australia whitewash: Bangladesh women slip to ninth in ICC ODI rankings
summary: A 3-0 series loss to Australia in Brisbane has caused the Bangladesh women's team to drop two places in the latest ICC Women's ODI rankings.
details: Bangladesh suffered a setback following an eight-wicket defeat to Australia in the third and final WODI in Brisbane on Wednesday.
The team was ranked seventh with 73 rating points before the start of the three-match series.
Following the 3-0 series whitewash, Bangladesh lost one rating point, causing them to slide down to ninth place.
Pakistan, who also had 73 points, moved up to seventh place, while the West Indies climbed to eighth with 72 points.
Australia remains the dominant force at the top of the rankings with 164 points, well clear of second-placed England with 126 points.
caption:
From 7th to 9th. A clean sweep by Australia has pushed the Bangladesh women's team down the ICC rankings.

Bangladesh suffered a setback following an eight-wicket defeat to Australia in the third and final WODI in Brisbane on Wednesday.

Pakistan, who also had 73 points, moved up to seventh place, while the West Indies climbed to eighth with 72 points.

headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being trafficked
summary: Victims were lured with high-paying construction jobs but forced into the Russian military and used as 'bait' in drone strikes.
details: At least 30 Bangladeshis were trafficked to Russia with promises of high-paying construction jobs, but were instead forced to join the Russian military and sent to the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) confirmed that 20 of these men have died. Seventeen of them were killed in drone strikes on their very first day of deployment.

Investigators believe the victims were used as 'bait' to reveal enemy positions. They were deployed to the battlefield after only 21 days of training, despite having no prior military experience or tactical skills.
The victims reportedly paid an average of Tk 10 lakh each to recruiting agencies, including Jabal-e-Noor, RS International, and TS Group, to secure the promised jobs.
Of the 10 survivors, two injured men have returned to Bangladesh, one of whom suffered lower-body paralysis after a drone strike and had to drag himself four kilometres to reach safety.
Two other survivors are receiving treatment in Moscow, while six remain on the battlefield. Most victims came from impoverished backgrounds and took out large loans to finance the trip.

The SRB has arrested two men, including the alleged mastermind Mizanur Rahman, on October 13. They are now searching for other syndicate members, including foreign nationals from Russia and Kyrgyzstan.
A separate investigation by Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds found that at least 104 Bangladeshis had been recruited into the Russian military by February 2026, with 34 reported dead.
caption:
Lured by promises of high-paying jobs, 30 Bangladeshis were trafficked to Russia and forced into war. 20 are dead.

At least 30 Bangladeshis were trafficked to Russia with promises of high-paying construction jobs, but were instead forced to join the Russian military and sent to the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war.

The Special Response Battalion (SRB) confirmed that 20 of these men have died. Seventeen of them were killed in drone strikes on their very first day of deployment.

Investigators believe the victims were used as 'bait' to reveal enemy positions. They were deployed to the battlefield after only 21 days of training, despite having no prior military experience or tactical skills.

The victims reportedly paid an average of Tk 10 lakh each to recruiting agencies, including Jabal-e-Noor, RS International, and TS Group, to secure the promised jobs.

Of the 10 survivors, two injured men have returned to Bangladesh, one of whom suffered lower-body paralysis after a drone strike and had to drag himself four kilometres to reach safety.

Two other survivors are receiving treatment in Moscow, while six remain on the battlefield. Most victims came from impoverished backgrounds and took out large loans to finance the trip.

The SRB has arrested two men, including the alleged mastermind Mizanur Rahman, on October 13. They are now searching for other syndicate members, including foreign nationals from Russia and Kyrgyzstan.

A separate investigation by Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds found that at least 104 Bangladeshis had been recruited into the Russian military by February 2026, with 34 reported dead.
